papers.title: Functional Femoral Slit Technique to Reduce the Length of ETO in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Case Series
papers.abstract: Introduction:In revision total hip arthroplasty, the femoral side mandates good intramedullary canal exposure to facilitate easy removal of a well-adhered implant and/or cement.This is achieved commonly through an extended trochanteric osteotomy (ETO).However, an ETO may compromise the minimum functional length of tubular middle third of diaphyseal bone that is essential for the reliable fixation of a fluted tapered titanium stem.To address this problem, we have developed the technique of functional femoral slit, which can be used to reduce the length of ETO so as not to compromise the fixation of the revision stem.The purpose of this study was to demonstrate the effectiveness of this innovative technique in various indications of revision of the femoral component. Case illustrations:We report a series of three cases of revision total hip replacement that required femoral stem revision.Two cases had aseptic loosening of stem with a snugly fitting distal cement.Third case was a broken cylindrical fully coated cementless stem with a well-integrated distal segment.Conclusion: Functional femoral slit successfully reduces the length of required ETO, preserves the cylindrical middle one-third diaphyseal bone, and gives adequate access to intramedullary canal.It is a versatile technique and can be used in multiple indications of femoral component revision.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文为临床病例系列，描述了全髋翻修术中的骨外科技术，未涉及AI、生物打印、FEA代理模型或增材制造，与用户研究方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper describes a surgical technique for revision THA and lacks any biomechanical modeling, implant design, FEA, AI/ML integration, or additive manufacturing context.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少翻修全髋关节置换术中延长截骨的长度，保留骨干固定区。
summary_zh.method: 介绍功能性股骨裂隙技术，通过三个病例展示其应用。
summary_zh.result: 该技术成功缩短了截骨长度，保留了骨干中1/3，提供了充分的髓腔暴露。
summary_zh.validation: 三个临床病例的系列报告。

summary_en.motivation: To preserve the diaphyseal bone stock required for stable fixation of revision femoral stems by reducing the length of extended trochanteric osteotomy.
summary_en.method: The functional femoral slit technique is described and demonstrated in three revision THA cases with different indications.
summary_en.result: The technique effectively shortens the osteotomy length and maintains the cylindrical middle-third diaphysis while providing adequate intramedullary access.
summary_en.validation: Three clinical case illustrations without comparative controls.

papers.title: Guarded Outcomes After Hip Hemiarthroplasty in Patients with Cerebral Palsy: Highlighting a Personalized Medicine Approach to Mitigate the Risk of Complications.
papers.abstract: Background: The effectiveness of hip hemiarthroplasty in managing femoral neck fractures in individuals with cerebral palsy has seldom been reported. Objectives: Given the complex neuromuscular issues associated with cerebral palsy (CP), this retrospective study aims to document the outcomes and characterize the complications of hip hemiarthroplasty for fractures of the femoral neck in a series of patients with CP, emphasizing the role of precision medicine in management. Methods: Six cases of hip hemiarthroplasty in six male patients with cerebral palsy and displaced femoral neck fractures have been reviewed in this study. The patients' mean age at the time of surgery was 55.6 ± 14.1 years (range, 33-71). All the patients were independent indoor ambulators before their femoral neck fracture and had various medical comorbidities. Five patients had intellectual disabilities. Results: The mean clinical and radiographic follow-ups for the patients included in this series were 91.5 and 71.3 months, respectively. All the patients developed significant heterotopic ossification (HO) around the operated hip, which was observed as early as the second week postoperatively on radiographs. HO progressed throughout the follow-up for all the patients. One patient had an early postoperative dislocation with femoral stem loosening, which was managed by implant revision. Another patient had an acetabular protrusion, leading to the loss of their weight-bearing ability and mobility due to pain. Four patients were deceased at a mean of 86.5 months after the index surgery. Conclusions: After considering the preliminary evidence provided with this small case series, this study suggests the overall guarded outcomes of hip hemiarthroplasty in patients with CP. Given the 100% rate of heterotopic ossification, a precision medicine framework with consideration for HO prophylaxis may be recommended after hip hemiarthroplasty in patients with CP. It may also be reasonable to scrutinize a personalized risk assessment approach in this patient subset regarding decision making, surgical approach, and rehabilitation program. The clinical outcomes and the risks of complications following hemiarthroplasty should be sensibly presented to patients with cerebral palsy and their caregivers to achieve reasonable postoperative expectations.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估脑瘫患者行髋关节半髋置换术的疗效及并发症。
summary_zh.method: 回顾分析6例脑瘫男性患者半髋置换术的临床与影像学资料。
summary_zh.result: 所有患者术后均出现异位骨化，并发症率高，结局不佳。
summary_zh.validation: 临床随访及影像学评估。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate outcomes and complications of hip hemiarthroplasty in patients with cerebral palsy, emphasizing personalized medicine.
summary_en.method: A retrospective review of six male cerebral palsy patients who underwent hip hemiarthroplasty for femoral neck fractures.
summary_en.result: All patients developed heterotopic ossification, with high complication rates and guarded long-term outcomes.
summary_en.validation: Clinical and radiographic follow-up with a mean of 91.5 and 71.3 months, respectively.
